ui.ctaSub: Check it in 5 seconds, free and private.

hub.title: Mic, Webcam, Sound & PC Troubleshooting Guides
hub.description: Step-by-step fixes for a mic, webcam, speakers, keyboard, mouse or screen that isn't working right. Windows, Mac, iPhone, Android, Discord and Zoom.
hub.lead: Short, practical fixes for the most common microphone, camera, sound, keyboard, mouse and screen problems. Test first, then follow the guide that matches what you see.

guides.title: Microphone Not Working on Windows 11 or 10? 9 Fixes
guides.description: Mic not working on Windows 11 or 10? Check privacy settings, the default input device, input volume, drivers and exclusive mode. Nine fixes, easiest first.
guides.h1: Microphone not working on Windows 11 or 10
guides.lead: Most Windows mic problems come down to one of three things: a privacy switch, the wrong default device, or input volume set to zero. Work through these in order. Each step takes under a minute.

p: Open the mic test on this site and press Start. If the level meter moves when you talk, your microphone and Windows are fine and the problem is inside one app (see the Discord, Zoom and Teams guide). If the meter stays flat, keep reading.
Windows can block every app from the mic with a single switch, and updates sometimes flip it off.
ol: Open Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone.
Turn on "Microphone access".
Turn on "Let apps access your microphone".
Scroll down and turn on "Let desktop apps access your microphone". Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Discord and Zoom all count as desktop apps.

p: If you have a webcam, a headset and a laptop mic, Windows may be listening to the wrong one.
ol: Open Settings → System → Sound.
Under Input, choose the microphone you actually speak into.
Talk and watch the small blue bar under "Input volume". If it moves, Windows hears you.

p: In the same Sound page, click your microphone and set Input volume to 80 or higher. A level of 0 to 10 looks exactly like a dead mic. If you have the option, leave "Enhance audio" off while you test, since some enhancement drivers mute quiet speech.

sections.h: 4. Check that the mic isn't disabled
p: Go to Settings → System → Sound → More sound settings → Recording tab. Right-click an empty area and tick "Show disabled devices". If your mic appears greyed out, right-click it and choose Enable.

ul: Laptops often have a mic-mute key (F4, F8 or a key with a crossed-out microphone). Its LED is usually lit when muted.
Headsets usually have a mute switch on the cable or a flip-to-mute boom arm.
USB mics like the Blue Yeti or HyperX QuadCast have their own mute button, which often glows red.

sections.h: 6. Plug it into the right port
p: On desktops, the pink 3.5 mm jack is the mic input. Headsets with a single 4-pole plug need a combo jack or a splitter. For USB mics, plug straight into the computer instead of a hub, then try a different port.

If the mic works in one app but goes silent in others, an app may have taken exclusive control. In More sound settings → Recording, open your mic's Properties → Advanced and untick both "Allow applications to take exclusive control" options.

sections.h: 8. Run the troubleshooter and update the driver
ol: Settings → System → Troubleshoot → Other troubleshooters → Recording Audio → Run.
Right-click Start → Device Manager → Audio inputs and outputs.
Right-click your microphone → Update driver. If that doesn't help, choose Uninstall device and restart. Windows reinstalls the driver on boot.

p: A full restart (not sleep) releases any app that's holding the mic. Afterwards, open the mic test again. If the meter still doesn't move with a known-good headset plugged in, the problem is likely the audio hardware or the port itself.

faq.q: Why does my mic work in Windows but not in my browser?
faq.a: The browser itself needs permission. Click the lock icon next to the address bar, set Microphone to Allow, and reload the page.

faq.q: Why is my mic so quiet on Windows?
faq.a: Input volume is usually set too low. Open Settings → System → Sound, click your input device and raise Input volume to 80 or more.

faq.q: My mic stopped working after a Windows update. What changed?
faq.a: Updates sometimes reset the privacy switches or the default device. Check steps 1 and 2 first.

guides.title: Mic or Camera Not Working on Mac? How to Fix It
guides.description: Mac microphone or camera not working? Fix privacy permissions, input device, input level and stuck camera processes on macOS Sonoma, Sequoia and later.
guides.h1: Microphone or camera not working on a Mac
guides.lead: On a Mac, almost every mic and camera problem is a permission that was never granted, or another app that is already using the camera. Here's how to sort it out.

p: Open the mic or webcam test on this site. If the browser can't see the device either, the fix is in System Settings below. If the test works but one app doesn't, the fix is in that app's own permissions.

sections.h: 1. Allow the app in Privacy & Security
ol: Open Apple menu → System Settings → Privacy & Security.
Click Microphone and turn on the switch next to your browser and any call app (Zoom, Teams, Discord).
Go back and do the same under Camera.
Quit and reopen the app. macOS only applies new permissions after a restart of the app.
p: If the app isn't listed at all, open it and try to use the mic once. macOS adds it to the list the first time it asks.

sections.h: 2. Choose the right input and raise the level
p: Open System Settings → Sound → Input. Select the microphone you use, then speak and watch the input level meter. Drag Input volume to around three quarters. AirPods and other Bluetooth headsets appear here too, and they often take over automatically when they connect.

sections.h: 3. Camera says it's in use, or shows black
ul: Close every app that might use the camera: FaceTime, Photo Booth, Zoom, Teams, OBS and other browser tabs.
The green light next to the camera turns on whenever something is using it. If it stays on with everything closed, restart the Mac.
If a restart isn't convenient, open Terminal and run sudo killall VDCAssistant, then try again. On newer macOS versions, sudo killall appleh13camerad does the same job on Apple silicon Macs.

sections.h: 4. Using an external webcam or USB mic
p: Plug it directly into the Mac rather than through a hub. Some USB-C hubs don't supply enough power for cameras. In call apps, pick the device by name in the app's video or audio settings. Many apps keep using the built-in camera until you change it.

sections.h: 5. Screen Time or a work profile is blocking it
p: Managed work Macs and Macs with Screen Time content restrictions can disable the camera. Check System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, or ask your IT team whether a profile is blocking it.

faq.q: Why doesn't Safari ask for camera permission?
faq.a: Open Safari → Settings → Websites → Camera (and Microphone) and set the site to Ask or Allow.

faq.q: How do I know which app is using my Mac's camera?
faq.a: Click the Control Center icon in the menu bar. When the camera or mic is in use, the app's name is shown at the top.

guides.title: Webcam Not Working? Fix a Black Screen or Missing Camera
guides.description: Webcam not working or showing a black screen? Fix privacy settings, the camera shutter, apps holding the camera, drivers and USB problems.
guides.h1: Webcam not working or showing a black screen
guides.lead: A webcam that shows nothing is usually blocked, busy or covered. Go through these checks in order. Most people are fixed by step 3.

p: Start the webcam test on this site. You'll get a clear result: no camera found, permission blocked, camera busy, or a working picture with its real resolution and frame rate. Use that result to jump to the right fix below.

Many laptops (Lenovo, HP, Dell) have a small sliding cover above the screen, and some have a camera kill switch on the side or a function key with a camera icon. A shutter gives you a black or grey image while the camera reports that it works fine.

sections.h: 2. Close other apps using the camera
p: On Windows, most webcams can only be used by one app at a time. Close Zoom, Teams, Skype, OBS, the Camera app and any other browser tab with a video call. Then reload the test.

ol: Windows: Settings → Privacy & security → Camera. Turn on "Camera access", "Let apps access your camera" and "Let desktop apps access your camera".
Mac: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera, then turn on your browser and call apps.
In the browser: click the lock icon next to the address bar, set Camera to Allow and reload.

sections.h: 4. Check the cable and port (USB webcams)
p: Plug the camera directly into the computer, not a hub or a monitor's USB port, and try another port. A 1080p webcam on a busy USB port can connect but deliver no frames.
If the picture freezes or stays black only at 1080p or 4K, switch to 720p in the test. If that works, the camera or the USB connection can't keep up at the higher setting.

ol: Right-click Start → Device Manager.
Open Cameras (or Imaging devices).
Right-click your webcam → Uninstall device, then restart. Windows installs a fresh driver on boot.
If the camera isn't listed at all, choose Action → Scan for hardware changes.

sections.h: Low FPS or a dark, grainy picture
p: Webcams slow their frame rate in dim light so each frame gets more exposure. Turn on a lamp in front of you, not behind you, and the FPS usually jumps back to 30. Also clean the lens. A smudge is the most common reason a picture looks soft.

faq.q: Why does my webcam work in one app but not another?
faq.a: Each app picks its own camera. Open that app's video settings and select your webcam by name. Also make sure no other app is holding it.

faq.q: Why is my webcam image mirrored?
faq.a: Preview images are mirrored so they feel like a mirror. Other people on the call see you the right way round.

guides.title: Mic Not Working in Discord, Zoom, Teams or Google Meet
guides.description: Others can't hear you on Discord, Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet? Pick the right input device, fix sensitivity and permissions. Fixes for each app.
guides.h1: Mic not working in Discord, Zoom, Teams or Google Meet
guides.lead: If your microphone passes the mic test here but nobody can hear you in a call, the problem is in the app. Each app keeps its own input setting, and it doesn't always follow Windows or macOS.

sections.h: First: test your mic outside the app
p: Run the mic test on this site with the same headset or microphone. If the meter moves, your hardware and system settings are fine. That narrows the fix down to the app settings below.

ol: Open User Settings (the gear next to your name) → Voice & Video.
Under Input Device, choose your microphone by name rather than "Default".
Use "Let's Check" to watch the level bar while you talk.
If you use Voice Activity, turn off "Automatically determine input sensitivity" and drag the slider left until your voice lights up the bar.
If nothing works, click "Reset Voice Settings" at the bottom of the page.
Open Settings → Audio.
Under Microphone, pick your device and press "Test Mic".
Untick "Automatically adjust microphone volume" if your level keeps dropping.
In a meeting, check that the mic icon at the bottom left isn't crossed out, and that the host hasn't muted everyone.
Click the three dots next to your profile picture → Settings → Devices.
Choose your microphone under Audio settings, then use "Make a test call" to record and hear yourself.
In the browser version, allow microphone access when the address bar asks.
In a meeting, click the three dots → Settings → Audio.
Pick your microphone and talk. The small dots next to its name should move.
If Meet says the mic is blocked, click the lock icon next to the address bar, set Microphone to Allow, and reload.

ul: Another app is holding the mic. Close OBS, other call apps and browser tabs, then rejoin.
You joined with "Computer audio" off or by phone. Rejoin with computer audio.
A Bluetooth headset switched to the wrong profile. Disconnect and reconnect it, then pick its "Headset" or "Hands-free" input.
Noise suppression is too aggressive. Lower it to Low or Auto and test again.

faq.q: Why can't people hear me on Discord when my mic works?
faq.a: Discord is probably using a different input device or the sensitivity threshold is too high. Choose your mic by name in Voice & Video and lower the input sensitivity.

faq.q: How do I test my mic before a Zoom call?
faq.a: Open the mic test on this site, or in Zoom go to Settings → Audio → Test Mic. Both take about five seconds.

guides.title: No Sound from Speakers or Headphones? 8 Fixes (Windows & Mac)
guides.description: No sound on your PC or Mac? Check the output device, volume mixer, cables, Bluetooth and drivers. Eight fixes for speakers and headphones, easiest first.
guides.h1: No sound from speakers or headphones
guides.lead: When a computer goes silent, it is almost always sending sound to the wrong device or has one volume slider at zero. Work through these checks in order. Most people hear sound again by step 3.

p: Open the speaker test on this site and play the left and right tones. If you hear them, your speakers and system are fine and the problem is inside one app or website. If you hear nothing, keep reading.

ul: The volume knob or buttons on the speakers or headphones themselves.
The mute key on the keyboard (often F1, F10 or a key with a crossed-out speaker).
The volume slider in the taskbar (Windows) or menu bar (Mac).
The volume inside the video player or website you are using.

p: Computers often have several outputs: laptop speakers, headphones, a monitor with speakers over HDMI, a USB headset and Bluetooth devices. Sound goes to only one of them.
ol: Windows: click the speaker icon in the taskbar, then the arrow next to the volume slider, and choose your speakers or headphones.
Mac: open System Settings → Sound → Output and choose your device.
Play the test tone again.

p: Windows keeps a separate volume for every app. Right-click the speaker icon → Open volume mixer, and make sure your browser or game is not muted or set to zero.

Push the plug all the way in. Wired headphones must go into the headphone (green) jack, not the microphone (pink) one. On a desktop, try the jack on the back of the PC, since front-panel jacks are sometimes not connected inside the case. For USB speakers and headsets, try another USB port directly on the computer.

ol: Turn Bluetooth off and on again.
If that does not help, remove (forget) the headphones in Bluetooth settings and pair them again.
On Windows, choose the "Headphones" or "Stereo" output, not "Headset" or "Hands-Free", for the best quality.

p: Go to Settings → System → Sound and click "Troubleshoot common sound problems" under Output. It restarts the audio service and fixes common driver settings automatically.

ol: Right-click Start → Device Manager.
Open "Sound, video and game controllers".
Right-click your audio device (Realtek, Intel, AMD or similar) → Uninstall device, then restart. Windows installs the driver again on boot.

p: If the Mac shows the right output but plays nothing, restart it. If sound still fails, open Activity Monitor, search for "coreaudiod" and quit it. macOS restarts it within a second.

Play the left and right tones in the speaker test. If one side is silent with every pair of headphones, check the balance slider (Windows: Settings → System → Sound → your device; Mac: Sound → Output → Balance). If only one pair is affected, the cable or plug is damaged.

faq.q: Why is there no sound on my computer even though the volume is up?
faq.a: Usually the sound is going to another output, such as a monitor over HDMI or a Bluetooth device that is off. Choose your speakers or headphones as the output device and test again.

faq.q: Why do my headphones work on my phone but not my PC?
faq.a: The PC is probably still sending sound to its speakers or a different output. Select the headphones as the output device. For wired headphones, use the green headphone jack.

faq.q: How do I test my speakers online?
faq.a: Open the speaker test on this site and play the left, right and sweep tones. You'll hear right away whether both channels and the low and high frequencies work.

guides.title: Mouse Double Clicking When You Click Once? How to Test & Fix
guides.description: Mouse double clicks on a single click? Test it in 30 seconds, then fix it: Windows settings, debounce, cleaning the switch, or using the warranty.
guides.h1: Mouse double clicking when you click once
guides.lead: A mouse that registers two clicks when you press once is one of the most common hardware faults. It is usually the switch under the button wearing out. Confirm it first, then try these fixes in order.

sections.h: Step 0: confirm it with a mouse test
p: Open the mouse test on this site and click normally for a minute. It flags any two clicks of the same button that arrive less than 80 milliseconds apart. Fingers cannot click that fast on purpose, so each flag is a fault. If you see flags, the mouse is double clicking. If not, check the Windows settings below.

Windows can be set to open files with a single click, which feels like a double click. Open File Explorer → View (or the three dots) → Options, and under "Click items as follows" choose "Double-click to open an item". Also check Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Mouse → Additional mouse settings, and set the double-click speed to the middle.

sections.h: 2. Try another USB port and turn off USB power saving
p: Plug the mouse directly into the computer instead of a hub. On a laptop, open Device Manager → Universal Serial Bus controllers, open each "USB Root Hub", and on the Power Management tab untick "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power".

Many gaming mice have a debounce or "click response" setting in their software (Logitech G HUB, Razer Synapse, SteelSeries GG and others). A very low value lets a worn switch send two clicks. Raise it a little, for example from 2 ms to 8 or 10 ms, and test again.
Unplug the mouse or remove the battery. Blow compressed air into the gap around the button while clicking it repeatedly for 20 to 30 seconds. Dust and grime can make the switch bounce.
Most mice have a warranty of 1 to 3 years, and double clicking is a recognized fault. Keep the result from the mouse test as proof when you contact support.

If you are comfortable opening the mouse and soldering, the switch under the button can be replaced for a few dollars. Look up your exact model first, since some mice use optical switches that do not wear out this way.

faq.q: Why does my mouse double click when I click once?
faq.a: Usually the metal contact inside the button's switch is worn or dirty, so one press makes it bounce and send two clicks. Settings such as single-click mode in Windows can also feel like a double click.

faq.q: How do I test if my mouse is double clicking?
faq.a: Open the mouse test on this site and click normally. Two clicks of the same button less than 80 ms apart are flagged as accidental double clicks.

faq.q: Can a double clicking mouse be fixed?
faq.a: Often yes. Raising the debounce time and cleaning the switch fix many mice. If it keeps happening, the switch needs replacing or the mouse is covered by warranty.

guides.title: Keyboard Keys Not Working or Typing Twice? 8 Fixes
guides.description: Some keys not working, typing twice or typing the wrong characters? Test every key, then fix Filter Keys, the layout, drivers, debris and chattering switches.
guides.h1: Keyboard keys not working or typing twice
guides.lead: When some keys do nothing, type twice or type the wrong letter, the cause is usually a setting, the keyboard layout or a dirty switch. Find out exactly which keys are affected first, then follow the fix that matches.

p: Open the keyboard test on this site and press every key once. Keys that never light up are not reaching the computer. Keys marked as chatter sent two presses for one. If a key types the wrong character but lights up in the right place, the problem is the layout (step 3), not the hardware.
Restart the computer. For a USB keyboard, plug it directly into the computer and try another port. For a wireless keyboard, replace or charge the batteries and pair it again.

sections.h: 2. Turn off Filter Keys and Sticky Keys (Windows)
p: Filter Keys ignores short or repeated presses, which looks exactly like keys not working. Open Settings → Accessibility → Keyboard and turn off Filter Keys and Sticky Keys. Holding the right Shift key for 8 seconds can switch Filter Keys on by accident.

If keys type the wrong symbols, for example @ and " are swapped or Y and Z are switched, the computer is using a different keyboard layout. Windows: press Windows + Space to switch, and remove layouts you don't use in Settings → Time & language → Language & region. Mac: System Settings → Keyboard → Input Sources.

sections.h: 4. Numbers not typing on the number pad?
p: Press Num Lock. On many laptops it is Fn + Num Lock or Fn + F11. When Num Lock is off, the number pad works as arrow keys instead.

ol: Unplug the keyboard or turn off the laptop.
Hold it upside down at an angle and tap it gently.
Blow compressed air under the stuck keys.
For a mechanical keyboard, pull off the keycap with a keycap puller and clean around the switch.

sections.h: 6. Fix a key that types twice (chatter)
p: A key that sends two presses for one is called chattering. On a mechanical keyboard, compressed air under the switch often fixes it, and on a hot-swap keyboard you can replace the switch in a minute. Many gaming keyboards also have a debounce setting in their software. Raising it slightly stops most chatter.

ol: Right-click Start → Device Manager.
Open Keyboards.
Right-click your keyboard → Uninstall device, then restart.

p: If keys still fail, the hardware is likely at fault. Try the keyboard on another computer. On a laptop, if the same keys fail in the BIOS screen too, the keyboard needs repair or replacement.

faq.q: Why are some keys on my keyboard not working?
faq.a: Common causes are Filter Keys being on, debris under the keys, a loose USB connection or a faulty switch. A key tester shows exactly which keys don't register.

faq.q: Why does my keyboard type two letters when I press once?
faq.a: That is key chatter: the switch bounces and sends two presses. Cleaning the switch or raising the debounce time usually fixes it. Otherwise the switch needs replacing.

faq.q: How do I test all the keys on my keyboard?
faq.a: Open the keyboard test on this site and press every key. Each key lights up when it registers, and the test also shows chatter and how many keys can be held at once.

guides.title: Dead or Stuck Pixel? How to Check Your Screen & Fix It
guides.description: Find dead and stuck pixels with solid color screens, learn the difference, and try the fixes that work: a flashing pixel fixer, gentle pressure, the warranty.
guides.h1: Dead or stuck pixel: how to check and fix it
guides.lead: A pixel that stays black, white or one bright color is easy to miss until it suddenly is all you see. Check a new screen as soon as you get it, because return windows are short. Here is how to find bad pixels and what you can do about them.

p: Wipe the screen with a dry microfiber cloth first. A speck of dust looks exactly like a dead pixel, but it moves or disappears when you wipe it.

Open the dead pixel test on this site and start full screen. It fills the display with black, white, red, green, blue and gray. Look at each color slowly from about 30 cm (one foot) away, section by section.

ul: Dead pixel: black on every color, most visible on white. The transistor gets no power and it is rarely fixable.
Stuck pixel: always one color (red, green or blue), most visible on black. Part of it is stuck on, and it can often be fixed.
Hot pixel: always white, visible on black. It is treated like a stuck pixel.

p: Stuck pixels can sometimes be revived by flashing colors rapidly over them. Open the pixel fixer in the dead pixel test, drag the flashing square over the stuck pixel and leave it running for 10 to 30 minutes. If it doesn't work the first time, try again for a few hours. Don't look at the flashing square if you are sensitive to flashing lights.

Turn the screen off, wrap a fingertip in a soft cloth, press very gently on the stuck spot and turn the screen on while pressing. Never press hard and never use anything pointed. This can make things worse on some panels, so try the pixel fixer first.

sections.h: 5. Check the warranty and return policy
p: Many manufacturers only replace a screen when it has a minimum number of bad pixels, but stores usually accept returns within 14 to 30 days for any reason. Take a photo of the pixel on the solid color and contact the seller quickly.

While you're testing a new monitor, the dead pixel test also measures its real refresh rate. If a 144 Hz monitor shows 60 Hz, set it in Windows under Settings → System → Display → Advanced display, and make sure you use a DisplayPort or a fast enough HDMI cable.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dead pixel and a stuck pixel?
faq.a: A dead pixel stays black on every color. A stuck pixel stays one color, usually red, green or blue. Stuck pixels can often be fixed, dead pixels rarely can.

faq.q: Can a stuck pixel fix itself?
faq.a: Sometimes, after hours or days of normal use. Running a flashing pixel fixer over it speeds this up and works for many stuck pixels.

faq.q: How do I check a new monitor for dead pixels?
faq.a: Clean the screen, then open a full-screen dead pixel test and look at solid black, white, red, green and blue. Do it on the first day so you can still return it.

guides.title: iPhone or Android Mic Not Working? 8 Fixes
guides.description: People can't hear you on calls, or your phone's mic is quiet or muffled? Fix app permissions, Bluetooth, the case and blocked openings on iPhone and Android.
guides.h1: iPhone or Android microphone not working
guides.lead: If people can't hear you, or your voice sounds quiet or muffled, the problem is usually a permission, a Bluetooth device or something covering the mic. Phones have more than one microphone, so test first to see which one is affected.

sections.h: Step 0: test the mic in your browser
p: Open the mic test on this site on your phone and press Start. If the level meter moves when you talk, the microphone works and the problem is in one app or in a call setting. If it stays flat, keep reading.
Phones switch to a connected Bluetooth headset, car or earbuds automatically, even if they are in your bag. Turn Bluetooth off and test again.

sections.h: 2. Allow microphone access for the app
ol: iPhone: Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then turn on the app.
Android: Settings → Apps → choose the app → Permissions → Microphone → Allow.
On Android 12 and later, also check that the microphone toggle in Quick Settings is not turned off.

sections.h: 3. Remove the case and screen protector
p: Cases and screen protectors can cover a microphone opening, especially after a drop shifts them. Remove them and test again.

Phones have mic openings at the bottom, near the camera and sometimes at the top. Gently clean them with a soft, dry toothbrush. Don't push pins or needles into the openings, since that can damage the mesh.

ul: Bottom mic: record a voice memo or voice recorder clip.
Front or top mic: record a selfie video.
Rear mic: record a video with the back camera.
If only one of them sounds muffled, that opening is blocked or damaged.

p: On iPhone, try switching Mic Mode in Control Center during a call (Standard, Voice Isolation, Wide Spectrum). On Android, turn off "Noise reduction" or "Clear voice" in the call settings, if your phone has them, and test again.
Restart the phone and install any system update. Bugs in the audio system are often fixed in updates.
Hold the power button, then press and hold "Power off" until you see Safe mode. If the mic works in safe mode, an app you installed is taking over the microphone.

faq.q: Why can't people hear me on calls but speakerphone works?
faq.a: Calls normally use the bottom microphone while speakerphone or video can use another one. Clean the bottom opening, remove the case and test again.

faq.q: How do I test my phone's microphone?
faq.a: Open the mic test on this site in your phone's browser, allow the microphone and talk. If the meter moves, the mic works. You can also record and play back a clip.

faq.q: Why is my phone mic muffled?
faq.a: Usually the case, a screen protector or lint is covering an opening. Remove them and gently clean the openings with a soft, dry brush.
